what.text: This page follows refugees from Afghanistan living in Pakistan.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1158538 Afghan refugees in Pakistan, 43.4% of all Afghan refugees and more than in any other host country.
In 2025 UNHCR also counted 140558 Afghans in Pakistan as other people in need of international protection, a separate group.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Afghanistan from 1978 to 2025, at war level for most of those years.
The groups fighting the government over that time include the Hizb-i Islami-yi Afghanistan, Jam'iyyat-i Islami-yi Afghanistan and the Taleban.
UCDP also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2015 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's figure for Pakistan rose from 1979 to its peak of 3272290 in 1989, then fell to 1043984 by 2006.
The main years of displacement in the data are 1981 to 1991, with shorter waves in 2000 and 2001, 2007 to 2012 and 2022 and 2023.
Returns from Pakistan to Afghanistan were highest in 2002 in UNHCR's returns data, and rose again in 2025.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees in Pakistan only, and UNHCR adds notes to some of them.
Pakistan's share of all Afghan refugees was 80.0% in 1979 and 43.4% in 2025.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
